Pastor nance graduated from trinity baptist college in 1992 with a bachelor of arts in pastoral theology and earned his master's degree in 2005. Please rise for the invocation and remain standing for the pledge of allegiance. Our Father, we're thankful today that we can come here and meet and assemble. Lord, we thank you so much for your hand of blessing that has been upon this city. Lord, we recognize even in this season with the hurricanes, how you have kept us and prevented us. Lord, we are very familiar with the danger in those storms. And, god, we recognize, lord, your favor upon that. Lord, we also recognize, lord, how you bless this city and, lord, that you have kept us and given us leadership, direction, growth, and, father, we just want to look to you for that and give you the honor and the praise. Lord, today, as we come to this meeting, lord, I do pray that you might bless these councilmen and women that sit here. Lord, we know that there are heavy decisions that they make and burdens that they carry. Lord, as they guide our city, I pray, lord, that you would give them wisdom. I pray that you would help them to have the judgments of the lord before them. God, I thank you that in the time of need that we are able to pray. Lord, I'm thankful that your ears are open. I thank you, lord, that you have a heart that loves us. So, god, would you guide them, would you be with them individually? Lord, even with their families, lord, the burdens they may carry there, would you give them grace? Lord, we pray for our mayor, that you overshadow her. Lord with the great decisions that are needed to be made. Lord, even with our police and our firemen, lord, as these men and women protect us and, lord, run into danger, god help them, be with them. Lord, the decisions they have to make. Lord, may your hand be with them. Lord, we just want to thank you today for your love, that your love is consistent, that it's faithful, that you never forsake us. Lord, that you demonstrated that love, lord, in the person of Jesus Christ. It's in his name we pray and ask. Amen. [Pledge of allegiance]

segments.text: Good morning, council. Good morning, council. So, today, I have the honor of presenting the commendation to lashaun tims. Tampa City Council is honored to present this commendation to lashaun tims, CEO and founder of 813 stop the violence. Lashaun is being recognized for her outstanding contributions as a role model, advocate, icon, and community advocate -- community activist in the Tampa Bay community. This commendation recognizes lashaun for her dedicated service and remarkable leadership in mentoring the youth and for being an individual who represents long-standing dedication to uplifting and advocating for our local Tampa Bay youth and for inspiring future generations through service, generosity, and positive leadership. Lashaun's work with the teen take-over initiatives, she helped transform the futures of nine young people who faced potentially life-altering felony convictions. Through her efforts of helping secure a six-week educational program, she helped these teens have their records cleared which gave them a second chance and ensure that one moment in their lives would not define the rest of their futures. Moreover, lashaun has become a pillar of strength and trusted voice in the community as she serves as a source of guidance and support for multiple families, navigating some of their most difficult moments. When gun violence impacts a family, lashaun is someone they know they can turn to and not only for answers, but for compassion, strength, and hope. Her work reflects the very best of our community. In gratitude to such great efforts, it is with great pleasure that the Tampa City Council presents this commendation on this 15th day of October, 2026, to lashaun tims. [ applause ] thank you. First, I will give honor to god. None of this would be possible without him. Right after thanking god, my heavenly mother, mama, thank you for teaching me it's okay to love. Okay to care about people even if you don't know them. That lesson lives in me and lives in the work I do every day. To my wife and my family, thank you for putting up with the commitment to the community. Thank you for understanding the long days, the phone calls, the cries, the pain, and all the times my heart was out there trying to help somebody else. It hasn't always been easy and I love you for standing beside me. My entire board, thank you for dealing with me and my orders. I have a vision. Thank you for helping to turn that vision into action. Thank you, Councilwoman Naya Young for this recognition. Thank you to Ms. Darlene for always answering the calls. Thank you to City Council for giving me this moment to share this journey. I want to take you back to 2014. I want to thank my mentor, state rep hart-lowman, for setting the stone for 813 stop the violence. Thank you to Kenya Robinson for allowing me to keep her son name alive. Nico Crawford was murdered in 2014. Thank you for the plans. Thank you for the walk. That walk mattered. One time, the work became even more personal. I met families living with grief. I met children who needed guidance, attention, hope. I saw so much need, kindness, and consistency. This wasn't just something I wanted to do anymore. It was something I knew I was called to do. 2025, I made 813 stop the violence a nonprofit. The paper work didn't make the mission. The mission was already in motion. Becoming a nonprofit gave the work another way to grow. 813 stop the violence tour. We go to neighborhoods and bring unity to the community. We create spaces where children can laugh, play games, role models and feel safe. We connect the families, resources and reminded people that their neighborhood mattered. Thank you freddy with safe and sound. It don't matter about the giveaways. It's about the conversation we happen to have when we are there. It's looking children in the eyes and saying, I see you and telling parents you're not alone. I stand here pretending that I don't -- that I have all the answers, but I don't. I can know that I cannot complain about our community and then refuse to work for change. Our children are watching. They need to see adults who keep their word, show up, and believe in their future. I'm going to keep showing up. I'm going to keep building partnership. I'm going to keep this tour into the neighborhoods. I'm going to keep working for young people and families. To all the angel moms and every parent who lost their child to gun violence, your pain is not forgotten. Your children matter. Their lives are why this work must continue. Every sponsor, volunteer, board member, community partner and family member who supported 813 stop the violence, INC., thank you. Once again, Councilwoman Naya Young, thank you for seeing the work and recognizing people behind it. This award is not just for me. It belongs to my family. Thank you, to every child, to everyone who supported 813 stop the violence. I started 813 in 2014. I made it a nonprofit in 2025. Here I stand in 2026 telling you we are just getting started. The work continues, the tour continues, the mission continues. We reach one, teach one, save one. No more silence. 813 stop the violence, INC., is more than an organization. It is a movement. We're going to keep moving. God bless you all. Thank you. Lashaun tims.

Residents need to understand this $80 million borrowed is more than $80 million paid back. At the interest rate and 30-year repayment period used in the published analysis, the total would be about 140 million. This is an estimate. It's not a final price, but interest is a real cost and residents deserve to see it. We are told taxes from future development will help repay the city. But the bills could arrive years before enough money comes in. The published model shows loan payments starting in 2027. The target forecast development revenue starts in 2031 but does not cover the full yearly payment until 2045. Think about that. The city would have bills to pay every year while waiting for the proposed development. So who covers that gap? If this deal pays for itself, show us who pays it until it does. If I take out a loan, I can't tell the bank, oh, my future business is going to cover that. They are going to want to know what I'm making right now, how I'll pay it right now. Tampa should do the same. Which city dollars will make those payments? What other projects could be delayed? Who pays if the development takes longer or brings in less money? The financing has a technical name. Non-ad valorem Bonds. That means loan relies on revenues other than property taxes. It does not mean there is no cost to the public. Before moving this forward, please give residents a simple year-by-year repayment plan. Show us loan payments, expected development revenue and exactly where the money comes from whenever there is a shortfall. If the rays are required to cover the shortfall, show us that, too. If they are not, say so clearly. Our neighborhoods need flood protection, safe streets, and reliable services today. $80 million commitment deserves more than a forecast.
